solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Prepared batter, a dip and something for kebab?

indicators.note: batter that is prepared has been made up, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook readies batter and a dip to go with a kebab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prepared' reshuffles BATTER, A and DIP together. The question mark admits the definition is by example: kebabs are often served in this flat bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat Middle Eastern bread is the usual wrapper for a doner kebab, so it is something that goes with one.

clue.text: Aviator sent back to the edge

indicators.note: something sent back goes the way it came, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: a lip is an edge or rim, as of a cup or cliff

explanation.surface: A flyer is ordered to return to the boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a pilot is the person flying an aircraft, an aviator.

clue.text: Ability to focus until venison is cooked

indicators.note: cooked food has been altered, and cooked figures are fiddled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chef can only concentrate until the venison is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: having a narrow single-minded concentration on one thing, ignoring all else, is often used as a near-compliment for focus.

clue.text: A boat going over border

indicators.note: in a down clue, going over means turning upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

explanation.surface: A vessel crosses a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' turns TUB upward to BUT. 'border' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to border on something is to lie right next to it and touch it.

clue.text: Call again in Yorkshire dialect

indicators.note: the letters sit in the run of the words Yorkshire dialect, across the gap

explanation.surface: Someone makes a second phone call speaking broad Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dial a phone number once more is to make a call again.

clue.text: Clear a mum or dad to adopt Penny

indicators.note: adopting takes someone into the family, so the parent letters take another letter inside

parts.note: either one is a parent
P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: A parent clears the way to adopt a girl named Penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to adopt' puts P inside A PARENT, just after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something plain to see or obvious is clear.

clue.text: Arrange some money for large piano

parts.note: to concert a plan is to arrange it jointly
a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: Someone sets about raising funds to buy a big piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Example of a type: the largest grand piano, built for concert halls, is a large piano.

clue.text: Tenant with lower entrance on the outside

parts.note: less is lower in amount

indicators.note: the letters on the outside of a word are its first and last

explanation.surface: A renter lives with a lower front door around the outside of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the outside' takes E and E, the ends of 'entrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person holding a property on a lease is a tenant.

clue.text: Scottish chap mostly seen in top lacking zip

indicators.note: a person seen in a hat is wearing it, so these letters go inside the others

parts.note: a lid is the top of a box or jar

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the name

parts.note: Angus is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: A sluggish Scotsman is spotted wearing a top hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the Scottish name, and 'seen in' means worn inside the top, as a head in a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: languid means listless and slow, without energy or zip.

clue.text: South coast resort where swimmers go, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken word, so the letters are a word that sounds like it

parts.note: swimmers go to a pool

explanation.surface: A seaside town said to be where swimmers head.
explanation.walkthrough: Poole is a seaside town in Dorset on England's south coast, said just like the swimmers' pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorset town with a large natural harbour is a south-coast English holiday resort.

clue.text: Online message that's short and sweet

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a tweet is a short message posted on Twitter, now X

explanation.surface: A brief, cute social media post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the last T of TWEET. 'short and sweet' is a phrase, but here 'sweet' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: twee is British for sickly cute or overly quaint, a pejorative sense of sweet.

clue.text: Military building's block with stretchers

definitions.note: read as 'military building is', the 's joining definition to wordplay

parts.note: to bar is to block
racks were instruments for stretching victims

explanation.surface: An army building is a block fitted with stretchers for the wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretchers' suggests the medical kind, but the rack was a torture device for stretching people.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: soldiers are housed in this building or set of buildings, treated as singular.

clue.text: Oxygen and neon, oxygen and neon — just the two of them

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
O again is the symbol for oxygen
Ne is the chemical symbol for neon

explanation.surface: A chemist lists two pairs of gases, oxygen and neon.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'neon' is taken as written and the second as its symbol NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting or contest between exactly two people, with nobody else, is just the two of them.

clue.text: Bird feeding intravenously

indicators.note: the letters are fed into the word intravenously, sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A sick bird being fed by drip.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large black crow is a bird.

clue.text: Censure reprocessed UK beer

indicators.note: something reprocessed is put through again and comes out changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Criticism of British beer that has been brewed again.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to reprimand someone sharply is to censure them.

clue.text: Last of Piesporter in smooth, round bottle

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the turned-around word
to turn round is to face the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: even means smooth and level

indicators.note: the final letter of the wine's name is taken

explanation.surface: A wine buff savours the end of a Piesporter in a smooth, rounded bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Piesporter is a German Moselle wine. 'round' turns EVEN into NEVE, and 'in' puts R inside it. 'bottle' is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: having bottle means having courage, the same as having nerve.

clue.text: Folk and pop feel contrived without force

indicators.note: something contrived is artificially worked up, so the letters are rearranged
without means the letter for force is taken away

parts.note: F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: Folk and pop music both have an artificial sound without any power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes F from POP FEEL, leaving POPEEL, and 'contrived' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: folk means people in general, as in 'ordinary folk'.

clue.text: Presented finest ring then got married

parts.note: best means finest
O is round like a ring
to wed is to get married; wed is also a past form

explanation.surface: Someone handed over the best ring and then married.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to bestow an honour or gift is to present it formally.

clue.text: Getting on with a good editor

explanation.surface: Getting along well with a good editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on' suggests getting along with someone, but here it means growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone getting on in years is growing old.

clue.text: Imagine some whisky around start of evening

indicators.note: the whisky goes around the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Picture a little whisky as the evening begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts DRAM around E, the 'start of evening'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to fancy or envisage something is to imagine it.

clue.text: Perhaps Queen Elizabeth's initial stake

parts.note: a queen is one example of an ant, the egg-laying one in a colony

indicators.note: the initial is the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: Queen Elizabeth might have had a first bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks royal, but 'Perhaps' signals an example: a queen ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker term: the stake each player puts in before the cards are dealt.

clue.text: Old Japanese capital Tokyo replaced

indicators.note: the letters of the name are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: Japan's old capital, which Tokyo superseded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' looks historical, as Tokyo did take over as capital, but it shuffles TOKYO.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical fact: the city was the imperial seat of Japan for over a thousand years before Tokyo.

clue.text: King tucked into exotic canape and more mundane food

indicators.note: the letter is tucked inside, put into the other letters
exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters change to an unfamiliar order

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch eats a fancy canape and plainer fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' suggests eating, but puts K into a reshuffle of CANAPE. 'more mundane' contrasts the answer with the canape.
explanation.definitionFit: Compared with an exotic canape, a flat batter cake is everyday food.

clue.text: Official in football final beset by hesitations making big decision?

parts.note: ref is short for referee, the football match official

indicators.note: beset means surrounded, so the hesitation letters go around the other word

parts.note: er and um are both sounds of hesitation
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: A football referee dithers before a big call in the cup final.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a national vote is only one kind of big decision.
explanation.definitionFit: A national vote on a single question is a big decision put to the whole electorate.
